reasons: Type definitions only, so there is no behaviour to test here.

terms.meaning: a list of parts that a piece of code must offer
a fake stand-in used in tests
a size level for the model, here fast or deep

sections.name: File setup, ModelTier
sections.title: Header and model tiers
sections.what: States the priority order (facts, then models, then language) and defines the two model tiers, fast and deep.
sections.why: Stated in the header: providers only phrase facts they are given.
sections.watch_out: A new tier must be added here and also in every provider's model settings.

sections.name: GenerateRequest, Usage
sections.title: Generation request
sections.what: Describes one request: a task name used for logs and templates, the system text, the input data, the expected output shape, the model tier, the token limit, and a template function that builds the same output without AI.
sections.why: The comments say the template is used without a key and as a fallback.
sections.watch_out: The template must return something matching the schema, or the fallback fails too.

sections.name: GenerateResult
sections.title: Generation result
sections.what: Describes what comes back: the checked output, which provider answered (gemini, template or mock), the model name, token usage, latency and cost. Cost is null when no price is set.
sections.why: Likely reason: logs and cost tracking can read one shape from any provider.
sections.watch_out: A null cost is not zero, so code that adds up costs must handle null.

sections.name: LlmProvider
sections.title: Provider rule
sections.what: The rule every provider must follow: a name, and a generate function that takes a request and returns a result.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app swap Gemini, the template or a test mock without changing callers.
sections.watch_out: Providers must throw errors rather than return partial results, because the fallback logic depends on errors.

summary: The shared contract that every text generator (Gemini, the template, and test mocks) must follow.
purpose: Let the rest of the app call one interface no matter which generator answers.
why: The header states the priority order: facts first, models second, language third, so providers only phrase facts they are given.
how: 1) A caller builds a generation request. 2) Any provider receives it. 3) The provider returns a result with the output and its details. 4) Failures are signalled by throwing an error.
inputs: Generation requests with task name, system text, input, expected schema, model tier, token limit and a template function.
outputs: Generation results with the checked output, provider name, model name, token usage, latency and cost.
risks: The interface checks nothing by itself; the checks happen in the schema and the verifier.
debug: If a type error names the provider, check it is one of gemini, template or mock. If cost is missing, check the price settings.
